title: Thermal-aware latency envelopes and runtime pin advisor for heterogeneous GPU SKUs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a thermal- and power-aware process to generate hardware-specific performance envelopes for A100/H100/L40S/MI300 variants and a runtime "pin advisor" that recommends per-model, per-sku pinning and degradation strategies based on thermal headroom and workload signals. Produce published profile artifacts that include thermal context tags, stability signatures, and canary gating metadata.
context: Existing hw profile workflows produce stable latency/cost signatures from benchmark runs, but we've seen tail regressions in production correlated with sustained power/thermal events on certain SKUs (notably A100 80GB and MI300 variants). Current profiles lack explicit thermal metadata and TTL semantics. Onboarding teams and the serving runtime need better guidance to avoid production regressions when GPUs thermally throttle or operate under different power caps.
proposal: 1) Extend perf profile artifact schema to include: thermal envelope (fan curve, ambient assumptions), sustained-power windows used during bench runs, and a stability score for cold/warm/tail behaviors. 2) Implement an offline 'thermal envelope generator' that replays representative sequences at multiple power caps and ambient thermals to synthesize an envelope (p50/p95/p99) for each SKU/model combo. 3) Build a runtime 'pin advisor' service that ingests live telemetry (GPU power, temperature, frequency) and suggests: auto-pin to robust variant, reduce batch size, enable prefix caching, or route to fallback variant. 4) Publish profiles with canary gating metadata (canary targets, smoke tests, roll-back triggers) to the profile catalog and surface recommendations in Console.
tradeoffs:
- More comprehensive profiles increase onboarding time and infra cost for perf runs.
- Runtime advisor adds complexity to request routing and increases surface for errors.
- Thermal-aware behavior may reduce throughput during sustained workloads to preserve tail SLAs; this impacts unit cost.
- We must avoid making pinning recommendations too conservative to prevent unnecessary cost increases for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Schema: Profile artifact schema extended and validated (thermal_tags, sustained_power_windows, stability_score) and accepted by model-onboard pipeline.

Generator: Thermal envelope generator produces reproducible p50/p95/p99 envelopes for A100/H100/L40S/MI300 on a representative sample of 6 models (LLM-7B, LLM-13B, open-chat-70B, quantized-13B, retriever-embed-2, reranker-small).
Runtime Advisor: Advisor prototype evaluates live telemetry and recommends pin/route decisions with <500ms decision latency in the staging environment.
Canary: Profiles published with canary metadata successfully gate rollout for at least two internal customers and auto-rollback when stability_score deteriorates >15% during canary window.
Documentation: Console UI surfaces thermal tags and advisor recommendations; onboarding doc updated with step-by-step authoring guidance.
Telemetry: New queries available that correlate thermal events to latency tails for postmortems (see telemetry_queries).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement schema changes and adapt model-onboard pipeline to accept thermal metadata. Run generator on a narrow model set in a test cluster.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Integrate runtime advisor prototype behind flag; route 5% of internal traffic for advisor recommendations only (no enforced routing).
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Enable advisory-driven canary for internal customers; gather stability metrics and tune thresholds.
Phase 4 (2 weeks): Flip advisor to automatic fallback for clearly unsafe states (e.g., sustained throttle + p99>target) for selected low-risk models; monitor cost/latency tradeoffs.
Phase 5: Publish profiles to catalog with TTL and canary metadata; update onboarding checklist and train SRE/solutions teams.
telemetry_queries: query: gpu_thermal_events_by_instance | filter sku in ("A100-80GB","MI300","H100","L40S") | group_by sku, model_variant | compute p99_latency_delta
query: sustained_power_windows | group_by node_id, sku | window 10m | count_throttles
test_plan: Runner tests: generator produces stable envelopes across 3 repeated runs within 5% variance at p95.
Staging advisor: decision latency <500ms and decision correctness (matches operator expectation) in 90% of audited cases.
Canary: auto-rollback triggers when stability_score drop >15% and is exercised during canary with synthetic thermal load.
Chaos test: simulate thermal event on MI300 node and verify advisor routes or pins as configured without request loss.

Consider exposing a simplified 'runtime health' score to customers in Console.
